title: Coffee Shop Google Ads Budget: How Much to Spend | DataLatte

facts.fact: The page recommends a coffee shop can start Google Ads at about $300 a month ($10 a day).
facts.quote: A coffee shop can start Google Ads at about $300 a month ($10 a day) and should raise it only when tracked calls, direction requests or orders pay back.

facts.fact: The page says that below about $200 a month a shop collects too few clicks to learn what works.
facts.quote: Below about $200 a month you collect too few clicks to learn what works, so treat the first two to three months as a test.

facts.fact: The page advises treating the first two to three months of Google Ads spending as a test period.
facts.quote: treat the first two to three months as a test.

facts.fact: According to WordStream by LocaliQ's 2026 benchmarks, the average cost per click for Restaurants & Food is $2.05.
facts.quote: For Restaurants & Food, WordStream by LocaliQ lists an average cost per click of $2.05

facts.quote: The all-industry averages are $5.42, 6.64%, 8.18% and $66.69.

facts.quote: The all-industry averages are $5.42, 6.64%, 8.18% and $66.69.

facts.fact: Google's monthly spending limit is 30.4 times the average daily budget.
facts.quote: Google's monthly spending limit is 30.4 times the average daily budget, so a $10 daily budget cannot cost more than $304 in a month.

facts.fact: On a given day a Google Ads campaign might spend up to twice its average daily budget.
facts.quote: On a given day a campaign might spend up to twice that amount

facts.fact: The page advises starting with at least $300 a month because much less often fails to produce enough data to optimize.
facts.quote: Pro tip: start with at least $300 a month. Much less than that often fails to produce enough data to optimize.

facts.fact: The page advises starting at a budget level that can be sustained for 8 to 12 weeks.
facts.quote: Start at a level you can sustain for 8 to 12 weeks.

facts.fact: The page suggests raising a profitable tracked-results budget gradually, by 10 to 20 percent at a time.
facts.quote: raise the budget gradually, for example by 10 to 20 percent at a time

facts.fact: The page defines a 'lead' as a conversion the account tracks, such as a call, a direction request or an order.
facts.quote: Here a "lead" is a conversion your account tracks, such as a call, a direction request or an order.

facts.fact: The page's daily budget figures divide the monthly budget by 30.4, the multiplier Google uses for its monthly spending limit.
facts.quote: Daily figures divide the month by 30.4, the multiplier Google uses for its monthly spending limit.

facts.fact: In the page's illustrative example, the assumed share of leads that become first-time customers is 40%.
facts.quote: Assume 40% of leads become a first-time customer

facts.fact: In the page's illustrative example, the assumed spend per visit by a new regular is $7 across 12 visits in three months.
facts.quote: assume a new regular spends $7 a visit across 12 visits in three months.

facts.fact: The page's $500 example assumes about 16 leads at the $30.57 benchmark cost per lead.
facts.quote: At the benchmark $30.57 per lead, that is about 16 leads.
